$comment: Build identity registry. Every address, offset, wire type and function name in this repository is only valid for the exact client build it was measured on, so a build must be identified before any of that evidence is reused. Identity is the full SHA-256 of Bin64/NewWorld.exe, never a short hash or a version string alone (AGENTS.md). Ghidra projects and corpora stay in the ignored reverse/builds/<sha256>/.

runtime_copy.relation_to_derived_from: The DTLS verify bypass of scripts/patch/patch-dtls-disk.py applied at VA 0x145DCF9F5 (0f 84 19 01 00 00 -> e9 1a 01 00 00 90), the 1.460 site, not the 1.400 site 0x145DCE8B5. Reproduced bit-exactly: `patch-dtls-disk.py restore` then `apply` on a clean 1.460 copy yields exactly this SHA-256, so this hash is the 1.460-plus-DTLS-patch copy and nothing else.
runtime_copy.relation_to_installed: THE SAME BUILD as the Steam source, plus the 5-byte DTLS patch. Both are 1.460.6033.6024067 and 179,214,008 B; they differ only at 0x145DCF9F5. This is the first time the lab and the static analysis have run the same binary, so every VA in the 1.460 entries of this file is valid for a live run. Never decompile this copy: read the Steam install instead, because this one's bytes are modified.

version_skew.was: The lab silently ran 1.400 (537403d4) while every named 1.460 address, and the DTLS site the launcher patches for 1.460 (0x145DCF9F5), belonged to 1.460. It persisted because Start-NwPrivate.ps1 records the copy as mode 'preserved' when its hash differs from Steam, and only replaces it on -RefreshExe or when the mode is 'synced' AND the runtime still matches its own recorded hash; private-client/state/client-source.json held exactly that.
version_skew.fix: `python scripts/patch/patch-dtls-disk.py restore` then `apply`, which re-patches the current install rather than reusing the stale copy, and then `Start-NwPrivate.ps1 -RefreshExe`. The resulting hash reproduced the value this file had recorded for the 1.460 copy all along (97f17df3), which is the proof the record and the bytes finally agree.
version_skew.guard_that_still_matters: build_sites.py::identify() refuses to patch when the private copy's size differs from the official one. That guard is what prevented the DTLS bypass from being applied at a 1.460 address inside a 1.400 binary, and it must stay.

consequence.statement: RESOLVED 2026-10-26. Static analysis reads the Steam install (30fe6461) and the lab now runs 30fe6461 plus the 5-byte DTLS patch (97f17df3), so a VA named from static analysis is valid for a live run. Every entry in client-functions.json and every offset in the client-map that carries build_sha256 30fe6461 may be used directly. The historical caveat applies only to the retained 1.400 entries (build_sha256 8654f01d), whose VAs belong to the previous build and must not be used against this one.
consequence.not_yet_done: UPDATED 2026-10-26 (second correction, same day). A Ghidra project for 30fe6461 NOW EXISTS: reverse/builds/30fe6461.../ghproj is 461 MB, imported in 96 s by `python ef.py re decompile --target 0x146455ec0` with -noanalysis, and it decompiles 1.460 functions on demand. The corpus is still only accounted (423,609 ranges, no shards); per-function decompilation works without it. The first four 1.460 functions are decompiled under reverse/builds/30fe6461.../functions/: selfident-1460.c (FUN_146455ec0, the 0x65c handler), selfident-consumer-1460.c (FUN_14167cc70), selfident-reader-1460.c (FUN_1417abe30), selfident-spawn-1460.c (FUN_141680460). What is still missing is per-message BODY decoding: the 0x65c struct layout is now proven from the handler, but its wire order is open by exactly one byte (see meanings.md).

rung_17_failure.note: The wall. The world sent the spawn six times - 0x8 bundles of exactly 46,407 bytes at seq 86, 89, 90, 91, 102 and 108 (plus 46,423 at seq 37), which is the size meanings.md records for the spawn. The client received them and never logged 'player spawn succeeds'. At 10:02:13.777 it gave up on its own: 'State(WaitingForPlayerSpawn) is timeout : frames 10, currentTimeoutIntervalCount 2', then ActorContainerDisconnect, 'Disconnected from REP', and 'CGame exiting to main menu'. So the captured 1.365 spawn satisfies 1.400 but NOT 1.460. No server-side disconnect and no crash: this is the client's own state timeout after ~120 s.
rung_17_failure.root_cause: ROOT CAUSE, measured 2026-10-26 with a controlled A/B. It is a RACE, not a missing field. The client's own log: '10:00:13.822 Loading of map "NewWorld_VitaeEterna" deferred in order to async unload previous level "NW_Frontend_NightHaven"' -> '10:00:13.831 HandleUnexpectedMessage skipping ReceiveStateBundle for bundle message due to clientContext == nullptr' -> '10:00:13.846 ...allowing map change' -> '10:00:13.846 Loading level NewWorld_VitaeEterna'. The spawn arrives 15 ms BEFORE the new level's context exists, so the client discards it, and the replay never repeats that seq. A/B: AZOTH_REPLAY_SPLIT_SEQ=0x25 (= replay seq 37, the 46,423-byte bundle) with AZOTH_REPLAY_SPLIT_DELAY_S=10 moved the drop to 10:25:04.485 and the map change to 10:25:04.503 (still 18 ms apart), but the client then kept the message: '10:25:04.939 ProcessPendingReliableMsgQueue processing 2 messages from m_pendingUnexpectedMsgs'. The rung still timed out at 10:26:54, so the split alone does not close it: only 2 messages were replayed out of the six large bundles, because the split holds seqs >= 0x25 and the rest of the spawn family never arrived late enough. This matches research/atlas/levers.md, which documents the identical 17 ms symptom and the 'replay split at 0x25' lever for 1.400. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PLAN: this is rig scheduling, NOT decompilation debt. No unnamed field is involved. Do not spend naming effort here.

wire-type-names.json.note: Regenerated 2026-10-25 after fixing four defects in scan-wire-names.py, which had been unrunnable since private-client/ moved to the repo root. Named rose from 2239 to 2559: 391 real names gained, 71 removed, and ZERO names that were already correct changed slot. Of the 71 removed, 39 MOVED to the correct slot (the name survived, the GUID it was attached to was wrong) and 32 were fragments that belong to nobody.
defects_fixed: ROOT resolved to reverse/ instead of the repo root, so every path was one level too high and the tool raised FileNotFoundError; the committed table had not been regenerated since the layout move.

_pick_name skipped any GUID-shaped run and kept looking. A BRACE belongs to the same descriptor and must be skipped, but a PLAIN dashed GUID is another descriptor's id, so the name further back is not this type's. Conflating them is how wire 449 stole 'AddActorMessage' from slot 121.
a printable run clipped by the 0x100 window, or split by PRINTABLE_RE's 110-char cap, was accepted as a name. That is where the fragment 'cc8a' came from for slot 0x5d1.

GUID_RE accepted only lowercase, so a type registered with an UPPERCASE dashed GUID was never indexed and its name belonged to nobody; a GUID up to 0xd0 bytes further along then picked it up. That is the root cause behind most of the 39 moved names.
wire-type-names.json.case_and_brace_rule: Case is the discriminator, measured on this image. A lowercase braced GUID IS a registration (<name> NUL <cvar> NUL {695842bb-...} -> slot 5037, PlayerArenaComponentServerFacet_RequestRemoteEnterDungeon). An UPPERCASE braced GUID is AZ's rendering of a GUID inside another descriptor's text (PingMsg NUL {85C7E01E-...} NUL <plain guid>) and must NOT be indexed, or it claims PingMsg and leaves wire 349 unnamed. The all-zero GUID is padding and is always skipped.

capture_purity.statement: pktmon runs with --comp nics, so a session pcap contains every flow on the machine, not only the game's. Measured on live_20261022_r1460_first: after the SNI fix the pcap named api.github.com, code.verboo.ai, telemetry.gentlemanprogramming.com, ecs.office.com, api.steampowered.com and store.steampowered.com, none of which the game contacts.
capture_purity.consequence: Flow attribution must be filtered by the game's PID connections or by the game's own host list before any traffic is treated as protocol evidence. A top-IP table from a raw pcap is not a game-flow table.
capture_purity.corrected_claim: The 22,273-packet TCP flow to 51.222.108.239 was first read as voice/Vivox from its OVH reverse DNS. With SNI extraction fixed it is code.verboo.ai, an agent-tooling host. The reverse-DNS inference was wrong.

After the one-line fix: 404 on the root and 200 on the tokens POST, and the gateway log shows 'POST /games/new-world/tokens 2B -> omni tokens mock'. Hostnames were never the problem: Caddy declares 34 and /etc/hosts maps all 34 to 127.0.0.1.

static_regeneration_2026_10_26.what: Full naming sweep of the 1.460 type table through the client's registration hook, the method proven in commit b7d106e and reversed into a tool this session (`python ef.py re message-names`).
static_regeneration_2026_10_26.comparison: The adjacency heuristic in research/derived/wire-type-names.json names 2559. The hook names 3390, and unlike adjacency it is compiler-written evidence. Of the replay's 40 types, the hook names 40/40.
static_regeneration_2026_10_26.no_guid_string_characterised: NOT a tool limitation. 40 of the 3565 were probed for their GUID in BOTH forms: the dashed text (either case) and the 16 raw bytes in AZ's little-endian-field order. Zero hits either way, so those GUIDs are absent from this executable. They are dead type-table slots this build never registers, not unnamed messages. That is why they resolve to nothing: there is nothing to find.
static_regeneration_2026_10_26.ambiguous_caveat: 796 types resolve to more than one name, because one GUID is reachable from more than one hook record. The first name is not necessarily the owner. Treat those as candidates and check the trait before relying on one.
